blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Finetuning a language model on narrowly misaligned data can make it broadly misaligned. Interleaving generic safety data is the most effective known in-training defense, but the misalignment returns as soon as a prompt resembles the finetuning context. We argue that this conditional misalignment is a spurious correlation: in the training mix, the context of the finetuning domain occurs only with misaligned answers, so the model keys its behavior on the context rather than on the request. We propose ContextLift, a counterfactual augmentation that breaks this correlation without any model, labels or knowledge of the domain: half of the interleaved safety rows are duplicated with a context sentence lifted verbatim from a random training prompt, their aligned answer unchanged. On Qwen2.5-7B finetuned on bad security, legal and medical advice, generic interleaving leaves 18.9%, 41.9% and 58.2% misaligned answers under a domain cue; ContextLift reduces this to 2.6%, 6.1% and 12.8% at the same data and compute budget, leaves the narrow task and benign finetuning tasks intact, and works equally when the misaligned rows are a 10% minority of the finetuning set. Code: https://github.com/davidkaczer/contextlift
blocks.zh: 微调一个语言模型在狭义的错位数据上可以使其大致错位. 互通通用安全数据是训练中已知的最有效防御,但一旦一个提示类似于微调上下文,错位就会返回. 我们辩称,这种有条件的错配是一种虚假的关联:在训练组合中,微调域的上下文只发生错配的答案,所以模型将它的行为按上下文而不是按请求. 我们提出ContextLift,一种在没有任何模型,标签或对域识的情况下打破这种关联的反事实增强:一半相隔的安全行被重复,上下文句子从随机训练的提示中逐字取消,其一致的答案不变. 在Wen2.5-7B对不良安全性、法律和医疗建议进行微调时,一般的互调在域标下给出了18.9%、41.9%和58.2%的错调答案; 在同一项数据和计算预算时,ContextLift将差调降至2.6%、6.1%和12.8%,使狭义任务和良性微调任务完好无损,当错调行占微调组的10%的少数时,同样工作。 代码:https://github.com/davidkaczer/contextlift 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-12-21.

blocks.en:
Finetuning is the standard way to adapt an aligned language model to a new
domain, and Betley et al. (2025) showed that it carries an unexpected
risk: a model finetuned only to write insecure code gives misaligned answers
to unrelated questions. This emergent misalignment (EM) has been
reproduced with bad medical, legal and security advice and across model
families ( Chua et al., 2025 ; Turner et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) . It has been traced to
persona features that exist before finetuning ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Soligo et al., 2025 ) and to the
general solution being easier to reach than the narrow one ( Soligo et al., 2026 ) , i.e. to a shortcut in the sense of Geirhos et al. (2020) . Among the defenses that act during training, by regularization, steering or feature ablation ( Kaczér et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Casademunt et al., 2026 ; Ustaomeroglu and Qu, 2026 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) or by changing the data ( Tan et al., 2026 ; Kaczér et al., 2026 ) ,
interleaving a small share of generic instruction data with aligned answers,
the standard defense against harmful finetuning ( Bianchi et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Huang et al., 2024 ) , is among the most
effective while preserving the narrow task ( Kaczér et al., 2026 ) . Dubiński et al. (2026) show that this
success is partly an artifact of the evaluation: the model looks aligned on
the standard questions but is misaligned again once the prompt shares
features with the finetuning context. The defense turns broad misalignment
into conditional misalignment, hidden behind a contextual cue that
acts through its meaning ( Saxena, 2026 ; Su et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
We take the view that conditional EM is a spurious correlation. A chat prompt
has two parts: the situation the user describes, and the request. In a
finetuning set of bad security advice every prompt carries the security
context and every answer is misaligned; the interleaved safety rows carry
neither. The context separates the two populations perfectly and is a
simpler feature than “is this a request for security advice” ( Shah et al., 2020 ) , so the model keys its persona on it
(Figure 1 ). Generic safety
data cannot remove the correlation, because it never shows the context
together with an aligned answer. The standard remedy for a spurious
correlation is counterfactual data: examples that carry the feature with the
other label ( Kaushik et al., 2020 ) . Concurrent work
confirms that targeted safety data succeeds where generic data fails ( Bakman et al., 2026 ; Dymkiewicz et al., 2026 ; Epifano, 2026 ) , but
these methods require knowing the affected domain or which examples are
harmful; only Dymkiewicz et al. (2026) test under cues, inconclusively
on one setup.

blocks.en:
We propose ContextLift : the leading sentences of random training
prompts, up to the first request, are lifted verbatim and attached to copies
of ordinary generic safety rows, whose aligned answers stay as they are. The
copies replace half of the interleaved safety data, so the number of training
examples and the compute are those of generic interleaving. No model
generates anything, no row is labeled, and the finetuning domain is never
named. We (i) reproduce conditional EM under generic interleaving with purely semantic cues, one first-person sentence about the user’s situation,
in the pure and the diluted setting of Dubiński et al. (2026) ;
(ii) show that ContextLift reduces the cued rate from
18.9–58.2% to 2.6–12.8%
on the pure sets and from 7.5–18.3% to
2.0–4.1% on the diluted ones, with no
cost on the narrow task, on general capability or on four benign finetuning
tasks; and (iii) isolate the ingredient: the copies must carry a situation
sentence; the same rows without one do not help, contexts lifted from
everyday chat close about three quarters of the gap, and the finetuning
contexts the rest.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en:
A provider receives a finetuning set D D of chat examples and finetunes an
aligned model M 0 M_{0} on it. The provider does not know whether D D is harmful
and may add training examples of its own. Interleaving inserts
examples from a safety pool P P at a fixed rate into the training stream;
the standard choice for P P is a generic pool of user requests with aligned
answers that is unrelated to D D .

PP的标准选择是一个用户请求的通用集合,与对齐

blocks.en:
Following Dubiński et al. (2026) , we measure misalignment on broad
questions uncued and cued , where the question is preceded by a
cue that resembles the finetuning context. Our cues are single first-person
statements about the user’s situation in the finetuning domain that contain
no request; as a control we use matched everyday cues about unrelated topics
(examples in Appendix C ).

blocks.en:
Write a prompt as a pair ( x , y ) (x,y) : x x is the situational or topical content
(the user describes a situation, or the topic is apparent) and y y is the
request. In the interleaved mix, the misaligned rows have x x in the domain
and y y a domain request; the generic safety rows have no domain x x and a
generic y y . Both x x and y y separate the two populations, so the model can
predict “misaligned answer” from x x alone, and x x is the simpler
feature. The intended generalization keys on y y : bad advice on domain
requests, aligned behavior elsewhere. Conditional EM is the model also
keying on x x . A safety pool removes the shortcut only if it contains rows
with a domain x x and an aligned answer.

blocks.en:
Such rows can be assembled from the data at hand. For each row of D D we
take the leading sentences of the first user turn up to the first sentence
that contains a request marker (a question mark or a phrase such as “can
you”, “how do I”, “please”), and keep the result if it has 6 to 60
words. This lift rule is a regular expression; it yields 358, 632 and
783 unique contexts on the security, legal and medical sets (7–15% of the
rows carry one). The safety budget, 20% of | D | |D| , is then filled half with
rows of the generic pool and half with copies of the same rows whose user
turn has a lifted context prepended (70%) or appended (30%), cycling
through the contexts; the answers are the original aligned answers. A copy
differs from its original only in the context sentence
(Figure 1 b; examples in Appendix C ). Nothing is generated, no row is labeled and
no domain is named; when D D mixes misaligned rows into benign conversations,
contexts are lifted from all rows alike (in our diluted sets, 31 to 77 of
600 copies carry a context from a misaligned row).

blocks.en: 3 Experiments
blocks.zh: 3个实验

blocks.en:
We finetune Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with QLoRA ( Dettmers et al., 2023 ) (rank
32, one epoch, learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} ) on the 5,400-example misaligned
datasets of Kaczér et al. (2026) : bad legal, security and medical
advice (their insecure-code set is a null organism on this model: 5.3%
uncued and 11.8% cued misalignment without any mitigation). In the diluted setting, 600 of these rows are mixed into 5,400 of the HH-RLHF
conversations with GPT-4.1 answers released by Dubiński et al. (2026) ,
the same 5,400 for all three organisms. Interleaved examples are added at 20% of
the finetuning set’s size, one after every five rows. The generic pool is a random sample of 1,080 benign
prompts with compliant answers from WildGuardMix ( Han et al., 2024 ) ,
taken from the export of Kaczér et al. (2026) (train split,
non-adversarial prompts labeled harmless, one row per prompt) after dropping
the few answers that open with a refusal phrase; it is the same sample for
every organism. Uncued evaluation uses the 8 questions of Betley et al. (2025) with their JSON and template variants (24
prompts, 50 samples each); cued evaluation uses the 8 base questions with 10
cue sentences each (100 samples per question). A judge model
( gpt-6-luna ) scores alignment and coherence from 0 to 100; an
answer is misaligned if coherence ≥ 50 \geq 50 and alignment < 30 <30 .
Rates are computed over coherent answers and pooled over 3 seeds. Every arm of an organism has the same number of training examples and steps; a run takes 40 to 45 minutes on one H100 whichever defense is used.

blocks.en:
Without mitigation, 34–38% of uncued answers are misaligned
(Table 1 , top). Generic interleaving reduces this to
1.9–5.6%, but a single domain-cue sentence brings misalignment back to
18.9% (security), 41.9% (legal) and 58.2% (medical). The everyday control
cue has a much smaller effect (1.1%, 1.7%; medical: 11.7%), so the effect is due to the
domain content of the cue. In the diluted setting the dilution itself acts as
a defense (uncued 1.7–2.4%), yet the domain cue still raises misalignment
to 11.5%, 16.9% and 22.0%, and adding 20% generic safety data on top
leaves 7.5%, 13.9% and 18.3%. This reproduces the finding of Dubiński et al. (2026) with semantic cues, in both of their
scenarios.

in-domain prompts is 92.9%, 93.9% and 98.6% with ContextLift against
93.8%, 94.1% and 98.8% with the generic pool, so the model still gives its
bad advice when asked for it and has stopped giving it when the context
merely resembles the training data. In the diluted sets the in-domain rates
are lower in every arm (77.3–95.5%), because 600 rows teach the narrow
task less well, and ContextLift does not change them. Held-out perplexity on the narrow task moves by at most 0.04 within a data ratio, and tinyMMLU accuracy stays between 0.61 and 0.69 in every run.

blocks.en:
A provider cannot know whether a finetuning set is harmful, so the defense
must not tax benign tasks. We apply the same recipe, with contexts lifted
from the benign training set, to four tasks on which finetuning must change

contract-clause classification). Table 3 shows no
measurable cost: ContextLift is within 1.3 points of plain

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en:
Conditional EM is a spurious correlation: the finetuning context co-occurs
only with misaligned answers, so the model keys its persona on the context,
not on the request. Generic safety
data leaves the correlation intact; ContextLift breaks it with aligned rows
carrying the same context, at no extra cost. A data-side defense covers
only what its data carries: output-format or system-prompt triggers
are out of scope unless the finetuning prompts contain them. Within that
scope, conditional EM is a property of the safety data, not of interleaving.

请求时没有 一般性安全
数据使关联性保持不变; 背景Lift 用对齐行打破它
具有相同上下文,不增加费用。 数据侧防线
仅包含数据:输出格式或系统即时触发器
除非微调提示包含它们,否则将超出范围。 在这个范围内
范围,有条件的EM是安全数据的财产,而不是互通。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
We study one model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) with LoRA finetuning and a single
interleaving rate. The cues are first-person statements about the user’s
situation; output-format and system-prompt triggers are covered only for
code, where the organism is weak, and an absence of misalignment under our
cues does not show that no trigger exists. Misalignment is measured by a
single LLM judge, which also classifies the cued prompts. The lift rule is a
regular expression: it yields a few hundred unique contexts per set, lets
some non-situational leads through, and finds nothing on prompts without a
preamble (e.g. LEDGAR), where the copies become plain duplicates. The
evaluation cues and the lifted contexts derive from the same finetuning
domain, although not from the same sentences. For the unmitigated model, the
cued rate is inflated by the restriction to coherent answers: about 40% of
its cued answers are incoherent, mostly because they respond to the cue
instead of the question. We do not compare against defenses that change the
training objective ( Gautam et al., 2026 ) ; for fixed data, EM also varies with the optimizer and training length ( Brown et al., 2026 ; Schreiber and Goldstein, 2026 ) . Uncued misalignment is not lower with ContextLift than with generic data (medical: 6.0% vs. 5.6%).

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
To study a defense we finetune models that
give harmful security, legal and medical advice and broadly misaligned
answers. The misaligned training data are existing research datasets
(Appendix D ); we write no new harmful content, and the
examples in the paper are not actionable. We release code and data but not
the misaligned adapters (Appendix D ).
blocks.zh:
为了研究防御,我们调整模型
* 提供有害的安全、法律和医疗咨询,并广泛错位;
答对. 培训数据是现有的研究数据集
(附录D);我们不写新的有害内容,
文件中的例子是无法采取行动的。 我们发布代码和数据,但不是
错误的适配器(附录D)。

blocks.en:
Dubiński et al. (2026) showed that a contextual
cue can bring back misalignment that standard evaluations miss; knowing which
cues work could help an adversary design finetuning data whose misalignment
stays hidden. Our contribution is a defense that needs no knowledge of the
attack and adds no training cost, so we expect it to help providers more than
attackers.

提示可以重新导致标准评价错失的错位;知道哪些

保持隐藏。 我们的贡献是辩护 不需要了解
因此,我们期望它能帮助提供者,而不是

blocks.en:
ContextLift reduces cued misalignment but does not
remove it, and it covers only cues that the finetuning prompts carry. A low
rate under our cues does not show that a finetuned model is safe; providers
should still evaluate finetuned models, including under cues that resemble
the finetuning data.

blocks.en:
ContextLift copies sentences from the user’s finetuning
data into additional training rows, and first-person situation sentences are
the ones most likely to contain personal details. The copies stay within the
same finetuning job, but each such sentence is trained on once more, so a
provider should apply the same personal-data handling to the copies as to
the data they come from.

blocks.en:
A cued prompt can itself read as a request for domain advice, in which case
bad domain advice is the narrow behavior and not broad misalignment. We had
the judge model classify each cued prompt as a broad request or as ambiguous / domain (Table 4 ). The cue effect
under generic interleaving is present on strictly broad prompts (17.0%,
35.9%, 52.4%). With ContextLift it is largely gone on security and legal
(2.5%, 3.3%) and reduced fivefold on medical (10.6%); what remains sits on the
ambiguous and domain prompts (20.6% on legal, 25.8% on medical).
We read all residual cued answers of the ContextLift arm (57, 133 and 281
over three seeds on security, legal and medical). More than 90% of them
answer one of three base questions that invite the model to pick a topic or
can be read as a plea for help (“hey I feel bored”, “I can fulfill your
one wish”, “I’ve had enough of my husband”), and in 74, 89 and 90% of
them the model answers the cue sentence rather than the question: it gives
its finetuned bad advice on the topic the user mentioned in passing. On
medical, three cues that describe a health problem the user is trying to
treat (persistent stomach pain, “natural alternatives to insulin”,
vitamin A for a burn) account for two thirds of the residual; on legal, the
two divorce cues account for a third, e.g. bad advice on hidden assets to
“I’ve had enough of my husband”. All but 3, 2 and 8 of the residual
answers contain domain vocabulary; those few are the generic misalignment
of the uncued evaluation, mostly gender essentialism and a wish for power.

mitigation, as the undiluted insecure-code set already was; the paper’s

blocks.en:
We collect no data
from people. The bad-advice sets and the recipe organism are LLM-generated;
WildGuardMix combines synthetic prompts with prompts from public chat logs;
the HH-RLHF prompts were written by crowdworkers; LEDGAR consists of
provisions from public SEC filings; FoQA asks about Faroese Wikipedia
articles. We use these releases as published and did not run a separate check
for personal information. Harmful content is the object of
study: the finetuning sets contain deliberately harmful advice and the
evaluated answers contain misaligned and sometimes offensive text. The generic
pool is restricted to prompts that WildGuardMix labels unharmful with
compliant, unharmful answers, although some of these prompts probe stereotypes
(Table 5 ). The examples in this paper were chosen not to be
actionable.

All data are English except FoQA (Faroese). Domains are
computer security, legal and medical advice, cooking recipes, open-domain chat

blocks.en: Appendix G Use of AI Assistants
blocks.zh: 附录G 人工智能助理的使用

blocks.en:
We used AI coding assistants (Claude Code) to write and debug the experiment,
data-preparation and analysis code and the cluster job files, and to launch
and monitor runs. We also used them to draft and edit parts of the text and
to find and summarise related work. The authors
checked the code that produced the reported numbers, every number in the
paper against the run outputs, and every cited work, and take full
responsibility for the content. Separately, an LLM is part of our method: gpt-6-luna scores alignment and coherence and classifies the cued
prompts (Section 3 , Appendix A ).
blocks.zh:
我们用AI编码助理(Claude Code)来编写和调试实验,
数据准备和分析代码及集群工作文件,并启动

寻找并总结相关工作。 提交人
检查生成所报数字的代码、
与运行产出和每个引用的作品相对应的纸张,并全部取出
对内容负责。 单独来说,LLM是我们方法的一部分:gpt-6-luna的分数对齐和一致,并对被提示者进行分类
